# Tables

Each table of addresses, jumps and words, entry by entry. An RTS table holds each target minus 1; the target column gives the target. Index: [the reference](index.md).

<a id="freq_table"></a>
## [`freq_table`](../../src/music/freq_table.asm#L6) `$9EBB-$A03A`

*words*

SID frequency table: 192 words, low byte first. Note byte n uses entry 2n (notes $00-$5f). The even entries are semitones in NTSC tuning (C0 = 16.35 Hz at 1022727 Hz). Each odd entry is the mean of its neighbours. The last word is $ffff. The driver adds the base $9ebb as two immediates at $9992 and $9d1f.

- **Read by:** [`start_note`](modules/music/tick.md#start_note) [`$9999`](../../src/music/tick.asm#L73), [`start_note`](modules/music/tick.md#start_note) [`$999F`](../../src/music/tick.asm#L76), [`effect_pitch_step`](modules/sound/effects.md#effect_pitch_step) [`$9D29`](../../src/sound/effects.asm#L82), [`effect_pitch_step`](modules/sound/effects.md#effect_pitch_step) [`$9D2F`](../../src/sound/effects.asm#L85)

<a id="tempo_latches"></a>
## [`tempo_latches`](../../src/music/driver_tables.asm#L12) `$A05B-$A07C`

*words*

CIA 1 timer B values for command $f6 (tempo), 17 words. Each value is 1000000 / ticks per second, for 16 to 80 ticks per second. A larger value gives a slower tune. The values assume 1 MHz: on a PAL C64 the music is 1.5% slower.
